problems: Minor: 'Mount Tabor' is a mountain, not a body of water, so it is a weak distractor. This does not make the item inaccurate or ambiguous.

Minor: the detail that the remnant took Jeremiah with them comes from Jeremiah 43:6 and is not in the supplied verse 7, but it is accurate KJV content. The note that Tahpanhes was a border city in the eastern Delta is extrabiblical but accurate. The hint narrows the region without giving the marker away.

Daniel 6:17 mentions the 'mouth of the den', but it does not say the opening was at the top. That location detail is added and unsupported by the cited verse; it is only arguably implied elsewhere, e.g. 'taken up out of the den' in 6:23. The verse also says a stone was laid on the mouth, so asking players to find an 'opening' is confusing: the object in the scene would be a sealed stone, not an open gap. The explanation slightly simplifies the sealing by omitting the lords' signet, which is minor. The prompt should be reworded to 'the mouth of the den' or 'the stone sealing the den', without the unsupported 'top' detail.

The cited verse (1 Kings 18:31) mentions only the twelve stones. The altar itself is not named until verse 32 ('with the stones he built an altar'). The reference label and hint point only to v31, while the explanation cites 31-32, so they do not match. The label should be 1 Kings 18:31-32 (or 18:32) so the altar is actually supported by the cited text.

The prompt asks for 'the men' (plural) who passed by, but the cited verse, Luke 10:31, mentions only the priest. The Levite appears in Luke 10:32, which is not in the reference label or the supplied KJV text. The hint points the player to 10:31 alone, which describes a single man. The explanation's citation (10:31-32) does not match the item's reference label. Either the reference should be Luke 10:31-32, or the prompt should ask for the priest only.

Genesis 8:19 never names elephants; elephants appear nowhere in the KJV. The item only works by assuming elephants fall under 'every beast', which is an extrapolation rather than something mentioned in or clearly implied by the verse. The explanation does not connect elephants to the text, so it does not support the prompt. The hint is also too vague to help. The prompt should target something the verse names, such as 'beasts', 'creeping things' or 'fowl'.

The explanation says Solomon set up the pillars, but the verse only says 'he'. In the context of 1 Kings 7:13-21, 'he' is Hiram of Tyre, the bronze worker who cast and set up the pillars. Naming Solomon misattributes the action in the cited passage. The object itself, the pillars, is clearly mentioned in the verse.

The hint gives the answer away. 'A pair of soldiers and a pair of restraints' restates the correct option almost word for word, and no other option mentions soldiers or restraints at all. The answer, distractors, explanation and clue are otherwise accurate to Acts 12:5-6. The clue's 'full watch' is a mild but acceptable embellishment.

The hint gives the answer away. It says the house belonged to the mother of a man surnamed Mark, and only one option mentions Mark, so the hint picks out the correct option on its own. The clue's phrase 'heard a familiar voice knocking at the gate' is also slightly garbled: Peter knocked, and Rhoda recognized his voice.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Seasonal work with a flock' fits only one option (shearing sheep), so the other three are eliminated immediately. The clue's wording 'tending to the flock' already points the same way, so the question becomes trivial. The clue also adds a minor detail, 'away from his tents', which the text does not state.

The hint gives the answer away outright. 'Think high, not low' rules out every option except the roof, and 'something she had laid out in order there' echoes the flax wording. The case and chapter title 'The Spies on the Roof' also reveals the answer to this stage. The answer itself is correct per Joshua 2:6, and 'under' versus 'with' the stalks of flax is acceptable paraphrase.
Minor: the case narrative calls the coat 'torn', which Genesis 37 does not say (only Jacob's claim that Joseph was 'rent in pieces'). This is outside the stage clue and does not affect this question.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Joshua the son of Nun' is the only option that names a father, so 'identified by his father's name' singles it out without the player reading the text. Minor point: the clue says the men were 'traced' to Rahab's house, which implies an investigation. The KJV says only that it was told the king; this is acceptable as mystery framing.

The hint gives the answer away. 'River crossing' is a direct paraphrase of 'unto the fords', and only one option mentions a river or ford. Players can pick it without knowing the text. A minor further issue: the clue's 'Gatekeeper's report' framing invents a gatekeeper source, although the verse only says 'they shut the gate'.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Freshly cut that had not yet dried out' is a near-paraphrase of 'green withs that were never dried,' and only one option mentions drying. The stage clue also states the answer outright ('Seven fresh, undried withs... Samson broke them'), so the question needs no reading of the text.

The hint gives the answer away. 'His head and a lifelong vow to God' paraphrases the correct option (no razor on his head; a Nazarite from his mother's womb), and that is the only option mentioning either his head or a vow, so the question becomes trivial. The answer, distractors, explanation and clue otherwise match Judges 16:15-17.

The stage clue gives the answer away outright: it says the first woman 'testified that they shared a home,' which is exactly the marked answer 'They dwelt together in one house.' A player can answer from the clue alone without engaging the text, so the stage has no puzzle value. The answer, distractors, explanation and hint are otherwise accurate to 1 Kings 3:16-17.

The hint gives the answer away. Saying the sum was 'pieces of a precious metal, but not gold' rules out the gold and field options and effectively says 'silver.' That leaves only 'Thirty pieces of silver' as an obvious match. The answer, explanation and clue are otherwise accurate to Matthew 26:14-16.

The hint effectively gives the answer away. It rules out 'Tribulation or persecution' and then says the thorns stand for 'two other pressures Jesus names.' The only remaining option naming two pressures is the correct one, so the player can answer by elimination without recalling the text. The hint also slightly overstates the text: Jesus says the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word; he does not explicitly say the thorns 'stand for' them.

The hint gives the answer away. Describing 'a small group' that 'approached Jesus away from the crowds' rules out the multitude, the Pharisees and the lone lawyer, leaving only the disciples 'privately' as the possible answer. The rest is accurate: the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25) is part of Jesus' reply to the disciples' private question on the mount of Olives in Matthew 24:3.

Minor: the hint says the phrase is 'at the end of the sentence', but the verse actually ends with 'and straightway took his journey'. The target phrase comes just before that, so this is slightly imprecise but not seriously misleading.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Open country' is essentially a synonym for 'wilderness', and every distractor (city, sheepfold at home, temple courts) is plainly not open country, so the hint settles the question by itself. It also adds a detail the text does not state: that the flock was grazing there.

The hint paraphrases the correct option almost element for element: 'her own house' (sweeps the house), 'needing light' (lights a candle) and 'carefully' (seeks diligently). It is also the only option set in the house, so the hint gives the answer away outright. The question, answer, distractors and explanation are otherwise accurate to Luke 15:8.

The hint gives the answer away outright. 'Think about storage space' points directly to the only option about storage ('no room where to bestow his fruits') and rules out the other three at once. The question, answer, and explanation are otherwise accurate to Luke 12:17.

The hint gives the answer away. Saying Jesus 'rejected Peter's number and gave a far larger one' rules out 'seven' and 'three'. The repayment option contains no number, so 'seventy times seven' is the only option left. The question, the marked answer and the explanation are otherwise accurate to Matthew 18:21-23.

The hint gives the answer away. 'A single coin for the day' rules out every distractor: two pence is two coins, a share of the vintage is not a coin, and a talent is a large sum or weight rather than a single coin paid daily. Only 'A penny a day' remains. The question, answer and explanation are otherwise accurate to Matthew 20:2.

The hint gives the answer away. It quotes the opening words "So likewise," and only the marked answer contains "likewise," so a player can pick it by word-matching without understanding the lesson. The question and answer are otherwise accurate to Matthew 18:35, and the distractors are clearly wrong.

Minor: the hint 'It is in the Old Testament' does not help, because every option is an Old Testament book. This is not disqualifying. Malachi 3:1 ('prepare the way before me') uses different wording, so it cannot be defended as a source of this verse.

The opening clause is echoed in Psalm 118:14 and Isaiah 12:2, but the full quoted verse, including 'I will prepare him an habitation; my father's God, and I will exalt him,' appears only in Exodus 15:2. The answer is therefore unambiguous. The hint is weak but does not give the answer away.

The quote matches KJV Hebrews 13:2, and no other option contains these words. Romans 12:13 and 1 Peter 4:9 speak of hospitality in different wording. The hint is weak because all four options are New Testament books, so it does not narrow the choice. It is not wrong, though, and does not give the answer away.
The hint is unhelpful because every option is a New Testament book, but it is not misleading and does not give the answer away.

The hint 'It is in 1 Peter.' gives the answer away outright, since 1 Peter 5:7 is the only option from 1 Peter. The quote, marked answer and explanation are otherwise accurate. Psalm 55:22 is thematically similar but uses different wording, so it is not a valid alternative.

Luke 11:9 (KJV) reads "And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." It contains the same quoted words as Matthew 7:7, so a player choosing Luke 11:9 could reasonably be defended, and the item is ambiguous. The hint "It is in Matthew" would separate the two, but it should not be needed to resolve a flawed distractor.
Minor: the title says 'The Miracles of Elisha', but the first event (asking for a double portion) is a request rather than a miracle. This does not affect the ordering.
Minor: the explanation cites only Numbers 14:34 for the forty years of wandering, but the word 'wander' is in 14:33. The clue passage includes 14:33-34, so this is acceptable.

Clue 1 says the items were taken 'from Jericho', but neither cited passage (Joshua 7:1, 7:21) names Jericho; they say only 'among the spoils' and 'the accursed thing'. The detail is true from Joshua 6 context but is not supported by the passages given. The hint 'Look in Joshua' nearly gives the answer away: Korah and Gehazi do not appear in Joshua, and Balaam is mentioned there only in passing.

Minor: clue 1's 'in Jerusalem' is not stated in Matthew 27:15-16, though the setting makes it clear. Clue 2 reasonably renders the ambiguous 'who had committed murder' as referring to the others. Neither issue causes ambiguity, and no other option fits the clues.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Whose promise holds even when keeping it hurts' is essentially a restatement of the marked option ('Keep your word… even though it now costs you'), so the player can match the hint to the answer without engaging with the verse. This is especially unsuitable for a difficulty-4 item.

The hint gives the answer away outright. It restates both parts of the correct option (contentment plus God's promise never to leave), so a player can match it without knowing the verse. The rest of the item is accurate: the marked answer matches Hebrews 13:5 KJV and the distractors are clearly contrary.

The hint gives the answer away. 'Each day already carries enough of its own' closely echoes the marked option's wording ('each day has enough trouble of its own'), so players can pick it by matching phrases rather than by understanding the verse. The distractors are also extreme and caricatured, which makes the item trivial even without the hint.

The hint gives the answer away. Saying Jesus lists 'four active things' points straight to the only option that lists four actions (love, bless, do good, pray), so no thought is needed. Minor issue: the explanation's quote ends at 'pray for them' with a closing quotation mark, which cuts off 'which despitefully use you, and persecute you' and presents a partial verse as the full saying.

The hint gives the answer away. It uses the word 'partial', which maps directly onto the marked option 'Show no partiality', and no other option contains that idea. The hint is also awkwardly worded: 'calls favoritism being partial' is ungrammatical and confusing for an adult player. The marked answer, the distractors and the explanation are otherwise accurate to the KJV text.

The hint gives the answer away. Its phrase 'not only your words but also your heart' maps directly onto the marked option, which is the only one that mentions the heart. It also rules out the main distractor ('Smile inwardly…'). Options B and D are plainly wrong, so the hint leaves effectively one choice, which is inappropriate for a difficulty-4 item. The answer and explanation are otherwise accurate to the KJV.
